title: Restriction of a locally quasi-finite morphism to open subschemes is locally quasi-finite (Stacks 01TH (4))
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Let $U\subseteq X$ and $V\subseteq S$ be open subschemes with $f(U)\subseteq V$, with inclusions $\iota_U:U\to X$, $\iota_V:V\to S$ (open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]), and let $f|_U:U\to V$ be the unique morphism with $\iota_V\circ f|_U=f\circ\iota_U$. Then $f|_U:U\to V$ is locally quasi-finite. (Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH, part (4): quasi-finiteness at a point may be checked on any pair of affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$, $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ with $f(\operatorname{Spec}A)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing the point; this is the 'local nature of local quasi-finiteness' invoked in the proof of Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03JA.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664, part (4) and its proof; Definition Tag 01TD (definition-quasi-finite), line 3538; as invoked in the proof of Lemma Tag 03JA, line 15495

proof.text: *$f$ is locally of finite type.* Since $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], it is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type].

source.place: Morphisms, remark after Definition Tag 01TD, line 3558

proof.text: *A small affine pair around a point.* Let $u\in U$ and $s=f(u)$; then $s\in V$ since $f(U)\subseteq V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] applied to $S$, the open $V$ and the point $s$, there is an open $V'\subseteq S$ with $s\in V'\subseteq V$ whose open subscheme is affine, $V'\cong\operatorname{Spec}R'$ with $R'=\mathcal O_S(V')$. The set $U\cap f^{-1}(V')$ is open in $X$ ($f$ is continuous) and contains $u$; by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] applied to $X$ there is an open $U'\subseteq X$ with $u\in U'\subseteq U\cap f^{-1}(V')$ whose open subscheme is affine, $U'\cong\operatorname{Spec}A'$ with $A'=\mathcal O_X(U')$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Then $u\in U'\subseteq U$, $V'\subseteq V$ and $f(U')\subseteq V'$.

*$f$ is quasi-finite at $u$ on the pair $(U',V')$.* By [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2), $f$ is quasi-finite at $u$, and $f$ is locally of finite type (step 1). Let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the fibre of $f$ at $s$ with first projection $p$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated] (Stacks 01TH, (1) implies (2)) the unique point $\xi\in X_s$ with $p(\xi)=u$ is isolated in $X_s$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs] (Stacks 01TH, (2) implies (4)) to $f$, the point $u$ and the affine opens $U'\ni u$, $V'$ of step 2 with $f(U')\subseteq V'$: the ring map $\varphi':R'=\mathcal O_S(V')\to A'=\mathcal O_X(U')$ induced by $f$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q'\subset A'$ corresponding to $u$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime].

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma Tag 01TH (lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize), line 3664: proof of (1) implies (2), lines 3684-3690, and of (2) implies (4), lines 3723-3726

proof.text: *The same pair for $f|_U$.* The open subscheme structure of $U$ is $\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_X|_U$ and that of $V$ is $\mathcal O_V=\mathcal O_S|_V$, and the inclusions $\iota_U,\iota_V$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] inducing the identity on sections over opens contained in $U$, resp. $V$. Hence $U'$, an open subset of $U$, has the same open subscheme $(U',\mathcal O_X|_{U'})$ whether regarded in $U$ or in $X$, so it is an affine open of $U$ with $\mathcal O_U(U')=A'$ and $u\in U'$; likewise $V'$ is an affine open of $V$ with $\mathcal O_V(V')=R'$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. As $\iota_V\circ f|_U=f\circ\iota_U$, the map $f|_U$ agrees with $f$ on underlying points, so $f|_U(U')=f(U')\subseteq V'$, and the ring map $\mathcal O_V(V')\to\mathcal O_U(U')$ induced by $f|_U$ equals the map $\varphi':\mathcal O_S(V')\to\mathcal O_X(U')$ induced by $f$ (compose with the identity maps on sections induced by $\iota_U$, $\iota_V$); the prime of $A'$ corresponding to $u$ is $\mathfrak q'$ in both cases. By step 3, $\varphi'$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q'$, so the pair $(U',V')$ witnesses that $f|_U:U\to V$ is quasi-finite at $u$ [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1).
*Conclusion.* Since $u\in U$ was arbitrary, $f|_U$ is quasi-finite at every point of $U$ (step 4), i.e. locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2).

split_report.summary: Read pqf-def-quasifinite: it takes the affine-local ring-theoretic definition of Stacks 01TD (1) (an affine pair Spec A ∋ x, Spec R with R -> A of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime of x), so the pair the definition gives need not lie in U, V and the proof must change the pair: that is Stacks 01TH, (1) => (2) => (4). Statement kept (checked against 01TD and 01TH (4)); stmt_deps kept. Proof in five steps: f is locally of finite type (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-lqf-locally-finite-type, the 'trivially' remark after 01TD, which rests on 01T2); choice of affine opens u ∈ U' ⊆ U ∩ f^{-1}(V'), s ∈ V' ⊆ V (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis, Stacks 01IT, Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens); u isolated in X_s by the existing lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-at-point-isolated (01TH (1)=>(2)) and then R' -> A' of finite type and quasi-finite at q' by the new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-quasi-finite-affine-pairs (01TH (2)=>(4), where 'isolated in X_s stays isolated in U_s' and U_s = Spec(A ⊗ κ(p)) belong); the ring map of f|_U on (U',V') is that of f (open subscheme structure sheaves are restrictions), giving quasi-finiteness of f|_U at u by 01TD (1). This route makes the fibre of f|_U unnecessary (only fibres of f occur). Mathlib: Mathlib's LocallyQuasiFinite (QuasiFinite.lean:71) omits locally of finite type, so the resLE instance (:132) is a candidate only, re-checked by sed. Searched the DAG for 01IT, 01T2, 01TH, 'isolated'/'quasi-finite at', 'locally quasi-finite'+'locally of finite type' before creating the three nodes.
